chunks: And from him, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Razīn, from Dharīḥ, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who inflicted upon another man a wound exposing the bone, and another inflicted upon him a bleeding wound in one and the same incident, then the man died. He said: “The diyyah is upon the two of them from their property, in two equal halves.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for wrongful killing or injury
key_terms.فِي مَقَامٍ وَاحِدٍ: in a single incident or circumstance
key_terms.مُوضِحَةً: a wound that exposes the bone

ai.seo_question: How is the diyyah divided when two people jointly wound a man and he dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding joint liability in a fatal assault involving two different head wounds inflicted in the same incident. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that when the victim dies, the diyyah is due from both assailants equally from their own property.
